1→# AI Site Engineer (AISE)
     2→
     3→## Quickstart
     4→
     5→Requires only Bun ≥ 1.2 (no Node, no Docker, no external services):
     6→
     7→```bash
     8→git clone https://github.com/payswapdotorg/AISE.git
     9→cd AISE
    10→bun install --frozen-lockfile
    11→bun run verify     # deterministic gate — must end VERIFY: PASS
    12→bun run dev        # web (http://localhost:5173) + API (http://127.0.0.1:8080), one Ctrl-C teardown
    13→```
    14→
    15→Other root commands: `bun run check:env` (environment validation),
    16→`bun run build` + `bun run start` (production-like local start — requires
    17→`AISE_DATA_DIR`, see docs), `bun run smoke` (end-to-end runtime smoke check
    18→on a scratch port). The authoritative guide — environment reference, ports,
    19→troubleshooting, and what is deliberately NOT included at this stage — is
    20→[`docs/INSTALL.md`](docs/INSTALL.md).
    21→
    22→## v2 Architecture Baseline — Capability-Aware Construction Reality Intelligence
    23→
    24→AISE is a cross-platform construction reality intelligence platform. It turns field evidence, documents, BOQs, drawings, specifications, measurements and device sensing into a versioned, evidence-linked engineering representation that people and AI can inspect, reason over, verify and use to plan interventions.
    25→
    26→The product is designed around one principle:
    27→
    28→> **The engineering assurance requirement is fixed by the task; the capture burden adapts to the capabilities of the device and the evidence already available.**
    29→
    30→AISE therefore does not pretend that every phone can produce the same quality of reconstruction. A higher-capability device may require less operator effort. A lower-capability device may require more guided capture, reference objects, manual measurements, additional evidence, or escalation to a better instrument/device. The system must never silently lower the assurance requirement because the device is weak.
    31→
    32→## Current status
    33→
    34→**Implementation campaign: complete — 41/41 governed v2 Work Items finalized.**
    35→
    36→The implementation layer is complete, but the repository is in a **post-implementation productization phase**. A provisional free-tier deployment has been evidenced at [`https://aise-tan.vercel.app`](https://aise-tan.vercel.app), but AISE is **not yet product-ready**. The latest evidenced deployed application commit is recorded in `docs/productization-state.json`; later repository changes do not imply that the public deployment contains those changes.
    37→
    38→The productization program is governed by:
    39→
    40→- `docs/productization-roadmap.md`
    41→- `docs/productization-work-orders.md`
    42→- `docs/PRODUCTION-READINESS-GATE.md`
    43→- `docs/free-tier-deployment.md`
    44→- `docs/INSTALL.md`
    45→- `docs/productization-state.json`
    46→- `docs/TECH-LEAD-HANDOFF.md`
    47→
    48→Only `PROD-015` may change the productization declaration to PRODUCT-READY.
    49→
    50→## Product promises
    51→
    52→### 1. Installable
    53→
    54→A fresh developer should be able to clone the repository, install dependencies with the checked-in lockfile, run the deterministic verification gate, start the product locally, and follow the demo flow using only repository documentation.
    55→
    56→### 2. Free-tier deployable
    57→
    58→The default evaluator deployment targets Vercel Hobby, Neon Free, Cloudflare R2 Standard and Upstash Redis Free, with Apify Free as an optional acquisition/import connector. Heavy reconstruction/GPU providers remain optional and are not required for the baseline demo journey.
    59→
    60→### 3. User-friendly interface
    61→
    62→The public product must present a coherent primary web experience for Projects, SiteTwin/Evidence, BOQ Lens, Engineering Case and Intervention Studio, plus the interactive engineering-solution workflow, with clear navigation and useful empty/error states.
    63→
    64→## Client architecture — one core, three adapters
    65→
    66→Browser, mobile and desktop are **adapters over the same AISE product/domain core**. They consume the same semantic task/capability contracts and may differ only in platform-specific presentation and interaction affordances.
    67→
    68→```text
    69→                 AISE PRODUCT / DOMAIN CORE
    70→   Reality | Evidence | Assurance | Verification | BOQ
    71→   Cases | Interventions | Outcomes | Solution Graph
    72→                           ▲
    73→                           │ shared capability/task contract
    74→          ┌────────────────┼────────────────┐
    75→          │                │                │
    76→       BROWSER           MOBILE          DESKTOP
    77→       ADAPTER           ADAPTER         ADAPTER
    78→```
    79→
    80→No client may own engineering readiness, canonical measurement authority, evidence sufficiency, verification, intervention approval, source-of-record authority or solution validation authority.
    81→
    82→## Product surfaces
    83→
    84→### BOQ Lens
    85→Makes BOQs understandable and operational. It connects BOQ sections/items, quantities, rates and cost scope to construction elements, locations, drawings, specifications and observed reality. A user can ask what a cost means, where the quantity is, what evidence supports it, what is missing, and what changed between revisions.
    86→
    87→### SiteTwin
    88→Creates a structured virtual representation of physical spaces and buildings from phones, depth sensors, LiDAR, photos, video, manual measurements and other evidence. It produces synchronized 2D, 3D and evidence views rather than a mesh-only deliverable.
    89→
    90→### Engineering Case
    91→Turns a site problem into a structured case: observations, measurements, material/condition information, uncertainty, evidence gaps, possible causes, engineering rules and review status.
    92→
    93→### Intervention Studio
    94→Represents proposed interventions as a sequence of model states. Each state can be viewed in 3D, 2D and BOQ views. A user can step through layers, inspect evidence and quantity/cost effects, and separate proposed changes from authoritative reality.
    95→
    96→### Interactive Engineering Solution
    97→This is a second first-class workflow for building problems. The user opens/reconstructs the current building and then constructs a proposed solution directly in an interactive environment or by natural-language commands to the integrated agent.
    98→
    99→```text
   100→CURRENT BUILDING REALITY
   101→        ↓
   102→ENGINEERING PROBLEM / INTENT
   103→        ↓
   104→INTERACTIVE SOLUTION
   105→        ↓
   106→DIRECT MANIPULATION / AGENT COMMANDS
   107→        ↓
   108→OPERATION 1 → PROPOSED STATE 1
   109→OPERATION 2 → PROPOSED STATE 2
   110→        ↓
   111→VALIDATE
   112→        ↓
   113→GENERATE SOLUTION BOQ
   114→        ↓
   115→BOQ LINE ↔ SOLUTION STEP / GEOMETRY
   116→```
   117→
   118→The environment is intended to feel as immediate and intuitive as a game while remaining a constrained engineering system: every consequential action becomes a typed engineering operation, deterministic geometry/quantity/validation services remain authoritative, and the proposal never overwrites observed reality.
   119→
   120→Example commands include:
   121→
   122→```text
   123→Excavate a pit 1.5 m deep, 2 m wide and 3 m long.
   124→Apply 30 mm plaster to the affected wall faces.
   125→Lay blocks up to 1 m high along this wall.
   126→```
   127→
   128→The integrated agent interprets such requests, asks for missing information and invokes deterministic operations. It does not invent dimensions/materials or bypass validation.
   129→
   130→A solution-generated BOQ is a versioned derived projection. Clicking a BOQ line should take the user to the contributing solution step/geometry; selecting a step should reveal the BOQ lines it creates or changes.
   131→
   132→**Phase 1 scope: buildings only.** The operation contract is intentionally extensible to future civil works, MEP, industrial equipment, electronics and integrated circuits.
   133→
   134→### Outcome Loop
   135→
   136→After work is performed, AISE captures the changed condition and outcome. This creates a trace from observed problem → diagnosis → proposed intervention → executed work → post-work evidence → observed outcome.
   137→
   138→## Integration-first adoption
   139→
   140→AISE is designed to become the primary engineering interface without demanding a rip-and-replace migration. Existing BIM, BOQ, CAD, project-management, ERP, procurement and document systems can remain systems of record while AISE exposes their context and authorized actions through connectors. Workflow migration is incremental, reversible and evidence-backed.
   141→
   142→AISE can also be plugged into `payswapdotorg/codex` as a vertical: Codex supplies agent/workflow orchestration while AISE remains authoritative for engineering reality, evidence, assurance, verification and BOQ semantics. The initial integration is external and requires no Codex-core modification.
   143→
   144→## Canonical lifecycle
   145→
   146→```text
   147→ENGINEERING INTENT
   148→        ↓
   149→ASSURANCE TARGET
   150→        ↓
   151→DEVICE + EVIDENCE CAPABILITY ASSESSMENT
   152→        ↓
   153→ADAPTIVE CAPTURE MISSION
   154→        ↓
   155→GUIDED MULTIMODAL CAPTURE
   156→        ↓
   157→RECONSTRUCTION STRATEGY SELECTION
   158→        ↓

    47→## Truth and uncertainty

1→# Architecture Change Record 005 — Interactive Engineering Solution Workflow
     2→
     3→**Status:** APPROVED
     4→**Architecture baseline:** 2.2 + ACR-004 client-adapter boundary
     5→
     6→## Decision
     7→
     8→AISE adds a second primary workflow alongside the existing reality/diagnosis/intervention/outcome workflow:
     9→
    10→```text
    11→CURRENT REALITY
    12→    ↓
    13→ENGINEERING PROBLEM / INTENT
    14→    ↓
    15→INTERACTIVE SOLUTION
    16→    ↓
    17→OPERATION STEPS
    18→    ↓
    19→VALIDATE
    20→    ↓
    21→GENERATE BOQ
    22→    ↓
    23→BOQ LINE ↔ SOLUTION STEP TRACEABILITY
    24→```
    25→
    26→The interactive solution is a versioned proposal built from authoritative observed/confirmed reality. It is not a game-world truth source and does not mutate observed reality.
    27→
    28→## Solution model
    29→
    30→Introduce a versioned **Solution Graph** composed of ordered `EngineeringOperation` records and resulting proposed states. Each operation is deterministic, typed, parameterized, spatially anchored and attributable to its source intent/user/agent.
    31→
    32→Phase 1 operations are for buildings and should prioritize deterministic, quantifiable operations such as excavation, demolition/removal, wall/block/brick placement, plaster/render/surface layers, simple slabs/foundations and supported building-service operations.
    33→
    34→## Interaction model
    35→
    36→The solution environment supports two equivalent input modes:
    37→
    38→1. **Direct manipulation:** select, place, move, resize, cut, remove, layer, inspect and step through operations using an interactive 3D/2D environment.
    39→2. **Agent command:** natural-language requests are translated into typed operation intents against the same operation contract.
    40→
    41→The agent is an interpreter/planner, not an engineering authority. Missing dimensions, materials, locations, sequencing or evidence must result in questions or explicit blocked states rather than invented facts.
    42→
    43→## Validation
    44→
    45→`Validate` is a deterministic server-side operation over the solution version. It may evaluate geometry, topology, units, quantities, operation ordering, modeled engineering rules, evidence/readiness constraints and unsupported/ambiguous operations.
    46→
    47→Validation produces explicit pass/fail/unknown/review-needed findings. A draft may remain editable, but a generated solution BOQ must be tied to a declared validation snapshot.
    48→
    49→## BOQ derivation and bidirectional navigation
    50→
    51→The solution BOQ is derived from the validated Solution Graph and proposed state deltas. Each generated line retains solution/version ID, contributing operation IDs, geometry references, units, calculation method, material/activity semantics, uncertainty and validation snapshot.
    52→
    53→Users must be able to navigate in both directions:
    54→
    55→```text
    56→BOQ line → corresponding operation(s) and geometry
    57→operation → generated/affected BOQ line(s)
    58→```
    59→
    60→The existing source BOQ remains separate and is never silently overwritten.
    61→
    62→## Architectural invariants
    63→
    64→- Reality Graph remains the canonical observed/confirmed engineering-model authority.
    65→- Evidence Graph remains the provenance authority.
    66→- Assurance Engine remains the task-readiness authority.
    67→- Verification Engine remains the deterministic verification authority.
    68→- Solution Graph is authoritative only for a proposed solution's operation/state history.
    69→- BOQ Graph remains a projection/domain representation.
    70→- LLMs/agents never directly become authoritative engineering executors.
    71→- All clients remain adapters over the same semantic operation/solution contracts.
    72→- Generated geometry is never labeled observed without evidence and acceptance.
    73→- Every operation is reproducible from versioned inputs and parameters.
    74→
    75→## Scope strategy
    76→
    77→Phase 1 is buildings only. The contracts must be domain-extensible so future verticals can add civil works, MEP, industrial machinery, electronics and integrated circuits without changing the client architecture or authority model.
    78→
    79→## Evidence requirement
    80→
    81→This is a CRITICAL change because it touches intervention simulation, geometry, quantities and verification. Implementation must provide deterministic tests, negative/discrimination tests, provenance tests and representative building/physical validation where engineering geometry or quantities are claimed.
    82→

     2→
     3→## Purpose
     4→
     5→Define the stable, domain-extensible contract for the interactive
     6→engineering solution workflow (ACR-005): the versioned Solution Graph of
     7→typed engineering operations and proposed states, the typed operation
     8→intents that direct manipulation and agent commands both compile into, the
     9→lifecycle/version/branch semantics of proposals, the operation capability
    10→negotiation, and the bidirectional solution-step ↔ generated-BOQ-line
    11→identity contracts.
    12→
    13→The contract is a proposal-authoring system, not a second reality system.
    14→The Solution Graph is canonical only for a proposed solution's

    17→
    18→## Checkable contract artifacts (PROD-021)
    19→
    20→This prose contract is formalized as a **versioned, testable contract
    21→package**: `packages/solution-contract/` (`@aise/solution-contract`),
    22→mirroring the `@aise/adapter-contract` discipline (TypeScript zod source of
    23→truth + committed self-contained draft-07 JSON Schemas + committed fixture
    24→corpus + deterministic schema-generation script).
    25→
    26→- **Contract version:** `SOLUTION_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1.0.0` (the package
    27→  version IS the contract version; every contract family — solution,
    28→  operation, state, validation, capability, trace, domain — ships it;
    29→  asserted by tests).
    30→- **The fourteen wire objects** (each a versioned, checkable wire object
    31→  with decode/decodeStrict/encode codecs, a committed JSON Schema and
    32→  committed fixtures):
    33→
    34→| Family | Wire objects |
    35→|---|---|
    36→| `solution` | `Solution`, `SolutionVersion` |
    37→| `operation` | `EngineeringOperation`, `EngineeringOperationIntent`, `OperationTarget`, `OperationDependency`, `OperationEffect` |
    38→| `state` | `ProposedState` |
    39→| `validation` | `SolutionValidationSnapshot` |
    40→| `capability` | `OperationCapabilityProfile`, `OperationCapabilityNegotiation` |
    41→| `trace` | `SolutionBoqLineTrace`, `SolutionBoqTraceSet` |
    42→| `domain` | `SolutionDomainDescriptor` |
    43→
    44→- **Regeneration / tests:** `cd packages/solution-contract && bun run
    45→  gen:schemas` regenerates the committed schemas byte-identically;
    46→  `bun test` runs the package's suite; the root `bun run verify` gate picks
    47→  the package up automatically.
    48→- **Compatibility window:** from the PROD-021 merge, the solution wave
    49→  workers (PROD-022 engine, PROD-023 agent compiler, PROD-025 BOQ
    50→  derivation) must not change this shared contract without a new governed
    51→  SHARED work item — see
    52→  `docs/productization-evidence/PROD-021/contract-artifacts.md`.
    53→
    54→## Solution graph objects
    55→
    56→```text
    57→AUTHORITATIVE OBSERVED / CONFIRMED REALITY (pinned baselineRealityVersionId)
    58→                 ↓
    59→           ProposedState 0        (baseline overlay)
    60→                 ↓ operation 1

    73→  current version pointer and the proposal-branch lineage.
    74→- **`SolutionVersion`** — one immutable versioned snapshot: the ORDERED
    75→  `EngineeringOperation` sequence and the resulting `ProposedState` array
    76→  (`states[N] = layer N`; `states.length === operations.length + 1`;
    77→  `states[0]` is the baseline overlay), the version lineage
    78→  (`parentVersionNumber`) and the declared validation snapshot when
    79→  validated.
    80→- **`EngineeringOperation`** — the typed, reproducible unit of the graph:
    81→  deterministic identity, version context (`solutionId`, `versionNumber`,
    82→  1-based `operationIndex`), open-vocabulary `operationType`, the vertical
    83→  descriptor, explicit typed parameters WITH units, a stable spatial
    84→  `OperationTarget` anchored to observed reality through read-only
    85→  references, `OperationDependency` precedence edges, engine-derived
    86→  `OperationEffect`s (state transitions + quantity impacts with typed units
    87→  and calculation provenance) and full `OperationProvenance`.
    88→- **`ProposedState`** — one proposed layer: the deterministic `stateId`
    89→  (the SAME identifier feeds the synchronized 3D/2D/BOQ views), the pinned
    90→  baseline, the literal `epistemicStatus: "PROPOSED"` seal, the ordered
    91→  applied operation ids and an optional content digest.
    92→
    93→## Operation intents and the two equivalent authoring modes
    94→
    95→`EngineeringOperationIntent` is the typed authoring object: explicit units
    96→(`TypedOperationParameter`: numeric values REQUIRE a unit), spatial target,
    97→parameters, dependencies and provenance (`origin: direct-manipulation |
    98→agent | imported-template`, attribution, evidence ids, the EXACT normalized
    99→agent `commandText`).
   100→
   101→`createOperationIntent(input)` is the ONE constructor surface for both
   102→modes. The SEMANTIC fields are identical regardless of origin; only the
   103→provenance differs. Because the deterministic identity derivation EXCLUDES
   104→provenance, the same semantics authored by direct manipulation or by an
   105→agent is the SAME operation (`deriveEngineeringOperationId` over both
   106→origins yields the same id — proven by the committed fixture pair and by
   107→tests). Authoring an intent is not authority: the server solution engine
   108→validates, negotiates capability, compiles and executes it; the agent may
   109→only translate, clarify and propose.
   110→
   111→## Deterministic identity rules
   112→
   113→Identities are content addresses (sha-256 over canonical JSON of a curated
   114→semantic projection — the intervention model's `deriveStateId` discipline):
   115→
   116→- **Operation identity** — version context + operation type + vertical +
   117→  typed parameters + spatial target + dependencies. Excluded by design:
   118→  provenance (origin, author, instant, command text, evidence),
   119→  rationale, descriptions, effects, timestamps and `contractVersion`
   120→  (a same-major minor bump must not re-address history).
   121→- **Proposed-state identity** — solutionId, versionNumber, stateIndex,
   122→  pinned baseline, ORDERED applied operation ids, content digest.
   123→  `materializedAt` excluded (identity is content, not the moment of
   124→  materialization).
   125→- **Validation-snapshot identity** — what the snapshot certifies:
   126→  solutionId, versionNumber, inputDigest, engine kind+version, outcome.
   127→- **BOQ-line-trace identity** — solutionId, versionNumber, boqLineId:
   128→  version-pinned by construction.
   129→
   130→## Lifecycle, version and branch semantics
   131→
   132→```text
   133→draft ────► validated ────► superseded   (terminal)
   134→  │             │
   135→  │             └─────────► abandoned    (terminal)
   136→  └───────────────────────► abandoned
   137→```
   138→
   139→`SOLUTION_LIFECYCLE_TRANSITIONS` is the governed table
   140→(`assertSolutionLifecycleTransition` enforces it with a typed error).
   141→Revision is versioning, never rewriting: editing creates a new
   142→`SolutionVersion` (with parent lineage) or a proposal branch (`Solution.branch`),
   143→and the superseding successor is named (`supersededBy`). The vocabulary
   144→carries NO approval semantics — approving an intervention is an Engineering
   145→Case domain act. A validated version must declare its validation snapshot
   146→(the BOQ generation gate); version 1 has no parent; a superseded solution
   147→names its successor (all invariant-checked).
   148→
   149→## Validation snapshots
   150→
   151→`Validate` is a server-side deterministic operation (PROD-022); this
   152→contract carries its RECORD: `SolutionValidationSnapshot` with the explicit
   153→findings (`checks`: `pass | fail | unknown | review-needed`, never empty),
   154→the worst-of `outcome` (fail > review-needed > unknown > pass —
   155→invariant-checked, helper `validationOutcomeWorstOf`), the `inputDigest`
   156→pinning the exact validated solution-version bytes, the engine identity and
   157→the deterministic snapshot id. A generated solution BOQ exists only tied to
   158→a declared validation snapshot of a validated solution version.
   159→
   160→## Operation capability negotiation
   161→
   162→`negotiateOperationCapability(intent, profile)` maps a typed intent and the
   163→ENGINE-owned `OperationCapabilityProfile` (per-vertical, per-operation-type
   164→honest statuses + required parameter names + limitations) to an explicit
   165→`OperationCapabilityNegotiation`:
   166→
   167→- `executable` — capability declared and all required parameters present
   168→  (with the degraded case's limitations surfaced);
   169→- `blocked` — the intent is underspecified: required parameters missing
   170→  (`missingParameters` in declaration order). The agent must ASK, never
   171→  invent;
   172→- `unsupported` — definitively not supported (a future vertical, an
   173→  undeclared operation type, an unavailable entry), with the honest reason
   174→  naming it;
   175→- `unknown` — capability undetermined (the frozen honesty discipline:
   176→  `unknown` is never conflated with `unsupported`).
   177→
   178→Unsupported-operation states are explicit, never silent; reasons are never
   179→empty. Negotiation is pure, deterministic, origin-blind and carries no
   180→validation/readiness/approval semantics — it changes execution strategy and
   181→operator/agent burden, never the truth standard.
   182→
   183→## BOQ derivation and bidirectional navigation
   184→
   185→```text
   186→BOQ line ──resolveOperationsForLine──► contributing solution steps
   187→solution step ──resolveLinesForOperation──► generated/affected BOQ lines
   188→```
   189→
   190→`SolutionBoqLineTrace` carries one generated line's full trace: the
   191→version-pinned contributing operations (`created | modified | removed` —
   192→never empty), the typed quantity (explicit unit + calculation reference +
   193→optional propagated uncertainty) and geometry references.
   194→`SolutionBoqTraceSet` is the version-pinned set generated from ONE declared
   195→validation snapshot; every line trace must pin the set's
   196→solutionId/versionNumber/snapshot (invariant-checked). Resolution in both
   197→directions is pure and the round trip closes (line → contributions → lines
   198→includes the original line — asserted over the committed fixture). A
   199→generated solution BOQ is a derived projection: the source BOQ remains a
   200→separate source/revision and is never silently overwritten.
   201→
   202→## Domain extensibility (Phase 1: buildings)
   203→
   204→Phase 1 is buildings only. The building specifics live behind
   205→`SolutionDomainDescriptor` (open `vertical` vocabulary with advisory value
   206→`building`; `operationVocabulary` naming the engine-owned catalogue;
   207→`extensions` as opaque data), and the wire `operationType` is an open
   208→string — the closed Phase 1 catalogue (ten types across site preparation,
   209→foundation, structure, enclosure, services, finishes) is reference data the
   210→ENGINE owns. **Nothing building-specific is encoded into client-facing
   211→types as authority.** The documented future verticals (civil-works, mep,
   212→industrial-equipment, electronics, integrated-circuits) are addable
   213→WITHOUT contract changes or client changes: their descriptors and intents
   214→are representable on the wire today, and an engine that does not declare
   215→capability for them negotiates to an explicit, honest `unsupported`.
   216→
   217→## No mutation of authoritative reality
   218→
   219→- The only reality references are read-only pins (`baselineRealityVersionId`
   220→  on `Solution` and every `ProposedState` — stable-id references).
   221→- The proposal seals are schema-level: `ProposedState.epistemicStatus` and
   222→  `Solution.epistemicClass` are the literal `"PROPOSED"`;
   223→  OBSERVED/INFERRED/CONFIRMED are unrepresentable inside a proposal.
   224→- The contract package exposes no mutation path for authoritative state;
   225→  the only client/agent-authored object is the intent (a request, never
   226→  authority). These invariants are discrimination-tested (typed-invalid
   227→  seal fixtures rejected; exported-name vocabulary and field-inventory
   228→  checks).
   229→- A proposal becomes observed reality only through execution, post-work
   230→  evidence and the existing assurance/verification process.
   231→
   232→## Conformance
   233→
   234→The contract's own checkable guarantees (byte-stable schema generation,
   235→codec version gate, fixture corpus validity, invariant cleanliness,
   236→identity re-derivation, negotiation determinism, bidirectional trace
   237→resolution, authority negatives) are enforced by the package's committed
   238→test suite; the root `bun run verify` gate runs them on every change. The
   239→PROD-022 engine and PROD-023 agent compiler consume this package as the
   240→operation contract; the PROD-024 adapter surfaces render its objects
   241→read-only.
   242→

1→# AISE Interactive Engineering Solution Workflow
     2→
     3→## Purpose
     4→
     5→AISE adds a second primary workflow alongside the existing reality/diagnosis/intervention/outcome workflow:
     6→
     7→```text
     8→CURRENT REALITY
     9→    ↓
    10→ENGINEERING PROBLEM / INTENT
    11→    ↓
    12→INTERACTIVE SOLUTION
    13→    ↓
    14→OPERATION STEPS
    15→    ↓
    16→VALIDATE
    17→    ↓
    18→GENERATE BOQ
    19→    ↓
    20→BOQ LINE ↔ SOLUTION STEP
    21→    ↓
    22→UNDERSTAND / REVIEW / MODIFY
    23→```
    24→
    25→The goal is to let a competent real-world engineer, technician, builder or other problem solver construct and inspect a proposed solution virtually with minimal specialist software knowledge.
    26→
    27→## Two equivalent authoring modes
    28→
    29→### Direct interaction
    30→
    31→The user works in a responsive 3D/2D environment with game-like interaction patterns:
    32→
    33→- select objects and locations;
    34→- place, move, resize, cut, remove and inspect;
    35→- excavate or fill volumes;
    36→- add construction/material layers;
    37→- step forward/backward through operations;
    38→- isolate a layer or affected area;
    39→- inspect quantities and constraints at the current step;
    40→- undo/revise an uncommitted proposal.
    41→
    42→The interaction should feel spatial and immediate, but it is not an unconstrained game engine. Every consequential action resolves to a typed engineering operation.
    43→
    44→### Natural-language interaction
    45→
    46→The same operations can be expressed to the integrated agent, for example:
    47→
    48→```text
    49→Excavate a pit 1.5 m deep, 2 m wide and 3 m long.
    50→Apply 30 mm plaster to the affected wall faces.
    51→Lay blocks to a height of 1 m along this wall.
    52→```
    53→
    54→The agent translates natural language into typed operation intents. It may ask for missing dimensions, material specification, location, sequencing or evidence. It cannot invent missing engineering facts or directly bypass validation.
    55→
    56→## Solution Graph
    57→
    58→A **Solution Graph** records the proposed solution as an ordered set of versioned `EngineeringOperation` records and resulting proposed states.
    59→
    60→An operation contains at minimum:
    61→
    62→- operation ID and solution/version ID;
    63→- operation type and parameters;
    64→- spatial targets and stable Reality Graph references;
    65→- input assumptions and required evidence;
    66→- dependencies/precedence;
    67→- geometry/state delta references;
    68→- quantity calculation references;
    69→- validation findings;
    70→- source (`user`, `agent`, `imported-template`, etc.);
    71→- provenance and timestamps.
    72→
    73→The Solution Graph is canonical for the proposal's operation/state history only. It is never canonical reality.
    74→
    75→## State model
    76→
    77→```text
    78→AUTHORITATIVE OBSERVED / CONFIRMED REALITY
    79→                    ↓
    80→             PROPOSED STATE 0
    81→                    ↓
    82→          OPERATION 1 → STATE 1
    83→                    ↓
    84→          OPERATION 2 → STATE 2
    85→                    ↓
    86→                ...
    87→                    ↓
    88→          OPERATION N → FINAL STATE
    89→```
    90→
    91→The original observed/confirmed reality remains immutable. Revisions create new solution versions or proposal branches rather than rewriting reality.
    92→
    93→## Validate
    94→
    95→`Validate` is a deterministic server-side operation. Depending on task and supported building domain, it evaluates:
    96→
    97→- geometry and dimensions;
    98→- topology/connectivity;
    99→- material/assembly compatibility where modeled;
   100→- units and quantity calculations;
   101→- operation ordering and dependencies;
   102→- known engineering rules represented in the verification system;
   103→- evidence/readiness constraints;
   104→- unsupported or ambiguous operations.
   105→
   106→Validation results must identify what passed, failed, is unknown, or requires additional evidence/review.
   107→
   108→A draft solution may exist before validation. A generated BOQ for the authoritative validated proposal must carry the exact validation snapshot and solution version from which it was generated.
   109→
   110→## BOQ generation and navigation
   111→
   112→After successful validation, AISE derives a solution BOQ from the Solution Graph and proposed state changes.
   113→
   114→Every generated BOQ line must retain bidirectional traceability to one or more solution operation IDs and their geometry/state references.
   115→
   116→```text
   117→BOQ line
   118→   ↓ click
   119→solution step / affected geometry
   120→
   121→solution step
   122→   ↓ inspect
   123→BOQ lines created or changed by this operation
   124→```
   125→
   126→The source BOQ, if one exists, remains a separate source/revision. A generated solution BOQ never silently overwrites it.
   127→
   128→## Initial building scope
   129→
   130→Phase 1 is **buildings only**. The underlying operation model is intentionally extensible so later domains can add civil works, MEP, industrial equipment, electronics and integrated circuits without changing the client architecture.
   131→
   132→The first building operation library should prioritize operations that can be represented and quantified deterministically, such as:
   133→
   134→- excavation and filling;
   135→- demolition/removal;
   136→- walls/block/brick placement;
   137→- plaster/render and surface layers;
   138→- slabs/foundations where supported by the validated model;
   139→- openings and simple construction assemblies;
   140→- selected building-service operations where already represented by the existing MEP foundation.
   141→
   142→High-risk or under-specified operations must stop at an explicit `needs_evidence`, `unsupported`, `requires_engineer_review` or equivalent state.
   143→
   144→## UX principle
   145→
   146→A person capable of solving the problem in reality should not need to learn AISE's internal terminology first. The product should present:
   147→
   148→```text
   149→What are you fixing?
   150→What does the current reality look like?
   151→What can you change?
   152→What will that change do?
   153→Is it valid?
   154→What will it cost / require?
   155→Where did that BOQ line come from?
   156→```
   157→
   158→The system exposes engineering constraints without exposing internal graph/service architecture as the primary interaction model.
   159→
   160→## Agent boundary
   161→
   162→The integrated agent is a planner, interpreter, explainer and tool user. It can:
   163→
   164→- translate text into operation intents;
   165→- propose operation sequences;
   166→- ask clarifying questions;
   167→- explain the effect of a step;
   168→- navigate the solution and BOQ;
   169→- call deterministic validation/quantity tools.
   170→
   171→It cannot:
   172→
   173→- declare observed reality;
   174→- declare readiness;
   175→- approve an intervention;
   176→- fabricate measurements or evidence;
   177→- bypass deterministic validation;
   178→- silently change a user's operation parameters;
   179→- turn a generated virtual result into observed evidence.
   180→
   181→## Cross-adapter requirement
   182→
   183→Browser, mobile and desktop remain adapters over the same Solution Graph and operation contracts. The operation semantics and validation outcomes are identical across adapters; only input/presentation affordances vary.
   184→
   185→The initial interactive authoring experience is expected to be richest on browser/desktop. Mobile can later expose a constrained field-oriented subset using the same operations.
   186→

1→# @aise/solution-engine
     2→
     3→The DETERMINISTIC INTERACTIVE SOLUTION ENGINE of the AISE interactive
     4→engineering solution workflow (Work Item PROD-022, CORE) — the
     5→server/domain engine that applies typed engineering operations to a
     6→proposed solution and produces reproducible proposed states, effects and
     7→quantities, per ACR-005/ACR-006 and `spec/solution-operation-contract.md`.
     8→
     9→**Pure deterministic computation over `@aise/solution-contract` objects.**
    10→No network, no clock reads (instants are caller-injected), no randomness,
    11→no environment-dependent output, no filesystem in the core — and **NO
    12→write path to authoritative reality**: the only window into the Reality
    13→Graph is the injected READ-ONLY `BaselineGeometryResolver` (one read
    14→method; the intervention service's `BaselineResolver` discipline).
    15→
    16→## Layout
    17→
    18→```text
    19→src/engine-version.ts        SOLUTION_ENGINE_KIND/VERSION + calculationRef
    20→src/errors.ts                typed outcomes + machine-readable reason codes
    21→src/units.ts                 deterministic unit vocabulary + exact conversions
    22→src/baseline.ts              the read-only baseline geometry seam
    23→src/quantity-models.ts       the Phase 1 building quantity calculus
    24→src/states.ts                state materialization + digest chain + transition ids
    25→src/apply.ts                 applyOperation (the core: intent → state delta)
    26→src/replay.ts                deterministic replay + injected clocks
    27→src/validation.ts            validateSolutionVersion (the server-side Validate)
    28→src/revise.ts                undo/revision via NEW versions (reviseVersion)
    29→src/quantities.ts            derived quantities of a state/version (raw, traced)
    30→src/index.ts                 public API (functions + frozen constants ONLY)
    31→src/*.test.ts                the deterministic + negative/discrimination suites
    32→src/testkit.ts               shared deterministic test-world builders
    33→scripts/generate-golden.ts   one-off golden-fixture generator (committed output)
    34→fixtures/                    committed engine fixtures (golden expected outputs)
    35→```
    36→
    37→Tests: `bun test` in this package (the root `bun run verify` gate picks
    38→them up automatically). No schemas are shipped here — the wire objects
    39→live in `@aise/solution-contract` (PROD-021, the shared contract).
    40→
    41→## What the engine does
    42→
    43→### Operation application + state-delta computation
    44→
    45→`applyOperation(input)` takes a baseline (a `ProposedState` or a
    46→`SolutionVersion`, whose LAST state is the baseline) plus a DECODED
    47→`EngineeringOperationIntent` and the ENGINE-OWNED
    48→`OperationCapabilityProfile`, and returns a typed
    49→`OperationApplicationResult`:
    50→
    51→- `applied` — the new version-pinned `ProposedState` (stateId via the
    52→  contract's `deriveProposedStateId`), the recorded
    53→  `EngineeringOperation` (operationId via the contract's
    54→  `deriveEngineeringOperationId`), the `OperationEffect`-shaped delta
    55→  (state transition + typed quantity impacts), the derived quantities
    56→  with full parameter traceability, the quantitative-limit findings and
    57→  the complete lineage (parent state, intent id, deterministic
    58→  transition identity);
    59→- `invalid` / `unsupported` / `needs-input` — the fail-closed outcomes,
    60→  every reason machine-readable (`EngineReason`).
    61→
    62→**Gating** uses the CONTRACT's `negotiateOperationCapability` (never a
    63→second negotiation semantics):
    64→
    65→| negotiation outcome | engine outcome | reason code |
    66→|---|---|---|
    67→| `executable` (possibly degraded) | `applied` (limitations surfaced in the echo) | — |
    68→| `blocked` (missing parameters) | `needs-input` | `missing_required_parameter` |
    69→| `unsupported` (definitive) | `unsupported` | `capability_unsupported` |
    70→| `unknown` (undetermined — never conflated) | `needs-input` | `capability_undetermined` |
    71→
    72→The engine additionally enforces, fail-closed: contract invariants
    73→(`intent_invariant_violation`), proposal-context consistency
    74→(`baseline_mismatch` — an intent is never silently re-targeted),
    75→dependency ordering (`dependency_not_applied`), unit rules
    76→(`unknown_unit`, `unit_dimension_mismatch`, `parameter_not_numeric`,
    77→`parameter_not_positive`, `missing_parameter_for_model`), duplicate
    78→operation identities (`duplicate_operation_in_state`) and coated-surface
    79→resolution (`surface_area_unresolved` — the engine ASKS, never invents a
    80→surface area).
    81→
    82→### Deterministic state materialization
    83→
    84→Every application materializes a NEW state (append-only — no in-place
    85→mutation exists). The state's `contentDigest` is a deterministic hash
    86→CHAIN (parent digest → layer index → operation id → canonical effect
    87→projection); `stateId` is derived through the contract's
    88→`deriveProposedStateId` (the SAME identifier feeds the synchronized
    89→3D/2D/BOQ views). `materializedAt` is caller-injected and EXCLUDED from
    90→identity. The transition identity (`lineage.transitionId`) is sha-256
    91→over the canonical transition content — the same content-addressing
    92→discipline as the contract's `identity.ts` (no second id format).
    93→
    94→### Undo/revision via NEW versions
    95→
    96→`reviseVersion({ version, revertOperationId, ... })` — "undo" — produces
    97→a NEW `SolutionVersion` (append-only lineage: parent + 1) whose
    98→operation sequence EXCLUDES the named operation (its effect reverts),
    99→rebuilds the kept operations through the SAME `applyOperation` path (new
   100→version context → new identities, provenance preserved verbatim,
   101→quantities recomputed), drops dependency edges that pointed at the
   102→reverted operation, and records the undo act as its own
   103→provenance-carrying `RevisionTransition` (who, why, when, deterministic
   104→transition identity). Destructive mutation of any historical version is
   105→structurally impossible: no API surface offers it, and the input version
   106→is consumed read-only (proven by the sabotage tests).
   107→
   108→### Deterministic validation
   109→
   110→`validateSolutionVersion(input)` — the server-side `Validate` of
   111→ACR-005 — runs the seven Phase 1 checks below and emits a CONTRACT-shaped
   112→`SolutionValidationSnapshot` (outcome via the contract's
   113→`validationOutcomeWorstOf`; snapshotId via the contract's
   114→`deriveValidationSnapshotId`; `inputDigest` = sha-256 of the version's
   115→canonical JSON bytes):
   116→
   117→1. `operation.contract-invariants` — the contract's own invariant
   118→   checkers over every operation, state and the version container →
   119→   **fail** on any finding;
   120→2. `geometry.dimensions-positive` — every numeric parameter strictly
   121→   positive → **fail** otherwise;
   122→3. `units.quantity-units-typed` — every numeric parameter's unit is in
   123→   the engine vocabulary and every quantity effect carries an explicit
   124→   unit → **fail** otherwise;
   125→4. `operation.ordering-dependencies` — dependency edges point backwards
   126→   in the sequence → **fail** on forward/self/unresolvable edges;
   127→5. `quantities.calculation-refs` — every quantity-impact effect carries
   128→   a calculation reference → **fail** otherwise;
   129→6. `operation.capability-declared` — every operation type declared by
   130→   the engine profile → **fail** on undeclared/unavailable, **unknown**
   131→   on undetermined capability (the frozen honesty discipline: unknown ≠
   132→   unsupported), pass with degraded limitations surfaced;
   133→7. `operation.phase1-limits` — the quantitative Phase 1 limits (below) →
   134→   **review-needed** on exceedance (the deterministic engineer-review
   135→   flag).
   136→
   137→Qualitative limitations ("load-bearing elements require engineer review
   138→before removal") are NOT validation checks: they are not computable from
   139→typed parameters and stay surfaced by the capability profile /
   140→negotiation reasons (rendered before any consequential action).
   141→
   142→### Deterministic replay
   143→
   144→`replaySolution(input)` reproduces the EXACT same solution/version/state
   145→chain, effects, quantities and transition identities for the same intent
   146→sequence — bit-identical canonical serialization via the contract codecs
   147→(proven against the committed golden fixtures). The ONLY time source is
   148→the injected `materializeClock: (stateIndex) => instant`
   149→(`fixedMaterializeClock` / `steppedMaterializeClock` helpers). A
   150→mid-sequence refusal fails the replay CLOSED at the named step with the
   151→refusal's machine-readable reasons. REPLAY DISCRIMINATION: two runs whose
   152→intents differ only in provenance metadata (author, authoredAt,
   153→commandText) produce IDENTICAL engine identities while preserving their
   154→distinct provenance — attribution is not semantics.
   155→
   156→### Derived quantities (raw, traced — the PROD-025 input)
   157→
   158→`deriveStateQuantities(version, stateIndex?)` aggregates the
   159→quantity-impact effects of operations 1..stateIndex (default: final
   160→state) into the per-operation inventory (each entry carrying the intent
   161→ref, operation id/index, SOURCE state id, resulting state id, parameter
   162→values+units, calculation ref and read-only geometry/node references)
   163→plus net totals per (dimension, unit). This is RAW operation/state
   164→QUANTITIES ONLY — BOQ lines, grouping and navigation are PROD-025's
   165→surface, built on exactly this inventory.
   166→
   167→## The quantity models (documented formulas)
   168→
   169→Canonical units: m, m2, m3, count (per the contract's
   170→`QuantityDimension` vocabulary). Parameter units convert EXACTLY (powers
   171→of ten: m/dm/cm/mm/km, m2/cm2/mm2, m3/cm3/mm3/l); unknown units and
   172→dimension mismatches fail closed. `calculationRef` =
   173→`aise-solution-engine/quantity/<operation-type>/v1`.
   174→
   175→| operation type | quantity | formula | direction |
   176→|---|---|---|---|
   177→| excavation | excavated-soil-volume | depth × width × length | removed (m3) |
   178→| excavation | excavation-footprint | width × length | removed (m2) |
   179→| backfill | backfill-volume | depth × width × length | added (m3) |
   180→| demolition-removal | removed-volume | length × height × thickness | removed (m3) |
   181→| demolition-removal | removed-face-area | length × height | removed (m2) |
   182→| foundation-placement | footing-volume | length × width × depth | added (m3) |
   183→| foundation-placement | footing-plan-area | length × width | added (m2) |
   184→| slab-placement | slab-volume | length × width × thickness | added (m3) |
   185→| slab-placement | slab-plan-area | length × width | added (m2) |
   186→| block-wall-placement | wall-volume | length × height × thickness | added (m3) |
   187→| block-wall-placement | wall-face-area | length × height | added (m2) |
   188→| block-wall-placement | block-count | ceil(height/0.2) × ceil(length/0.4) | added (count) |
   189→| opening-creation | opening-area | width × height | removed (m2) |
   190→| opening-creation | opening-count | 1 per operation | added (count) |
   191→| plaster-application | plaster-area | resolved baseline target surface area | added (m2) |
   192→| plaster-application | plaster-volume | surface area × thickness | added (m3) |
   193→| finish-application | finish-area | resolved baseline target surface area | added (m2) |
   194→| finish-application | finish-volume | surface area × thickness | added (m3) |
   195→| building-service-installation | service-run-length | length | added (m) |
   196→| building-service-installation | service-run-count | 1 per operation | added (count) |
   197→
   198→**Where the engineering model does not yet define a quantity** (Phase 1
   199→has no `packages/engineering-model` quantity model), the engine ships
   200→the SIMPLEST DEFENSIBLE DETERMINISTIC formula as versioned reference
   201→data, never hidden in code:
   202→
   203→- **Block module** — nominal module face 400 × 200 mm INCLUDING 10 mm
   204→  joints (`DEFAULT_BLOCK_MODULE_LENGTH/HEIGHT`); a partial module at a
   205→  course end or a partial top course counts as a whole block (ceiling).
   206→  Example: 5 m × 1 m wall → 5 courses × 13 modules = **65 blocks**.
   207→- **Coated surface area** — plaster/finish coat AREA is an anchored
   208→  target property, resolved through the READ-ONLY
   209→  `BaselineGeometryResolver` (a `surface_area_unresolved` target is an
   210→  honest needs-input state — the engine never invents an area).
   211→- **Quantitative Phase 1 limits** (mirroring the reference capability
   212→  profile's declared limitation strings, as data —
   213→  `REFERENCE_BUILDING_OPERATION_LIMITS`): excavation depth ≤ 6 m;
   214→  block-wall height ≤ 3 m; plaster thickness ≤ 50 mm per coat.
   215→  Exceedance is a deterministic REVIEW-NEEDED validation finding, not a
   216→  silent pass and not a fabrication.
   217→
   218→The WHOLE model set is SWAPPABLE behind the `QuantityModel` interface
   219→(`quantityModels` input on apply/replay/validate/revise) — a future
   220→engineering model can replace any entry without touching the engine
   221→core, as long as the replacement stays deterministic.
   222→
   223→## Fixtures
   224→
   225→`fixtures/` (committed, deterministic):
   226→
   227→- `baseline-geometry.json` — the demo wall world's read-only surface
   228→  facts (geo-wall-faces-002 → 12.5 m2, …);
   229→- `wall-upgrade-expected.json` — the GOLDEN replay of the contract
   230→  corpus's wall-upgrade intents (demolition → block wall → plaster):
   231→  states, digests, operation ids, transition ids, per-step quantities,
   232→  the validation snapshot and the quantity inventory, regenerated by
   233→  `bun scripts/generate-golden.ts` (the tests assert byte-identical
   234→  reproduction);
   235→- `engine-quantity-expectations.json` — the quantity inventory of all
   236→  TEN Phase 1 building operation types (operation → formula → expected
   237→  value), from the contract's committed intent fixtures.
   238→
   239→The intent corpus itself is REUSED BY REFERENCE from
   240→`packages/solution-contract/fixtures/operation/` (the testkit loads the
   241→contract's committed fixtures — including the direct-manipulation vs
   242→agent pair, the blocked/unsupported/unknown negotiation cases and the
   243→future-vertical case).
   244→
   245→## Reason-code inventory (fail-closed outcomes)
   246→
   247→`invalid`: `intent_invariant_violation`, `unknown_unit`,
   248→`unit_dimension_mismatch`, `parameter_not_numeric`,
   249→`parameter_not_positive`, `missing_parameter_for_model`,
   250→`dependency_not_applied`, `operation_index_mismatch`,
   251→`baseline_mismatch`, `duplicate_operation_in_state` ·
   252→`unsupported`: `capability_unsupported` · `needs-input`:
   253→`missing_required_parameter`, `capability_undetermined`,
   254→`surface_area_unresolved` · revision refusals: `version_terminal`,
   255→`unknown_operation_to_revert`, `revision_not_appendable`.
   256→Every refusal carries a non-empty machine-readable reason — never a
   257→silent drop, never a best-effort.
   258→
   259→## Consumption
   260→
   261→```ts
   262→import {
   263→  applyOperation, replaySolution, validateSolutionVersion, reviseVersion,
   264→  deriveStateQuantities, TableBaselineGeometryResolver,
   265→  REFERENCE_BUILDING_OPERATION_PROFILE,
   266→} from "@aise/solution-engine";
   267→```
   268→
   269→The backend transport surface lives in `backend/api/src/solution/`
   270→(model / service / router — a pure route factory following the
   271→`execution/` exemplar). The engine package imports ONLY
   272→`@aise/solution-contract`, `@aise/shared-contracts` and `node:crypto` —
   273→never `apps/**` or `backend/**` (workspace boundary rules).
   274→
   275→## Non-goals (owned by other work items)
   276→
   277→- The operation intent CONTRACT (PROD-021 — consumed, never modified).
   278→- The agent operation compiler / interaction loop (PROD-023).
   279→- The interactive 3D/2D environment (PROD-024).
   280→- BOQ line derivation, grouping, cost and navigation (PROD-025 — the
   281→  engine provides the raw traced quantities only).
   282→- Server persistence, transport wiring and authorization (backend work
   283→  items; the Tech Lead mounts the route factory).
   284→

     2→ * Engineering operation intent (PROD-021) — family `operation`.
     3→ *
     4→ * THE TYPED INTENT OBJECT with explicit units, spatial target, parameters
     5→ * and provenance. `createOperationIntent` is the ONE constructor surface for

     7→ *
     8→ *  - DIRECT MANIPULATION: `provenance.origin: "direct-manipulation"` with an
     9→ *    optional `interactionDetail` (what the operator did in the interactive
    10→ *    environment);
    11→ *  - AGENT COMMAND: `provenance.origin: "agent"` with the EXACT normalized
    12→ *    `commandText` ("Excavate a pit 1.5 m deep, 2 m wide and 3 m long.").
    13→ *
    14→ * The SEMANTIC fields (operationType, domain, parameters, target, dependsOn)
    15→ * are IDENTICAL regardless of origin; only the provenance differs. Because
    16→ * identity derivations EXCLUDE provenance (identity.ts), the same semantics
    17→ * authored by direct manipulation or an agent IS THE SAME OPERATION — the
    18→ * acceptance criterion "same operation intent can be produced by direct
    19→ * manipulation or an agent" is structural, and proven by the committed
    20→ * fixture pair
    21→ * `fixtures/operation/EngineeringOperationIntent.valid-excavation-direct.json`
    22→ * vs `...valid-excavation-agent.json` (asserted by identity.test.ts and
    23→ * fixtures.test.ts).
    24→ *
    25→ * AUTHORING AN INTENT IS NOT AUTHORITY: an intent expresses what the author
    26→ * wants done. The server solution engine (PROD-022) validates, negotiates
    27→ * capability (negotiation.ts), compiles and executes it; the agent (PROD-023)
    28→ * may only translate, clarify and propose. The intent deliberately CANNOT
    29→ * express validation outcomes, readiness, approval or any epistemic claim
    30→ * over observed reality (asserted by authority.test.ts).

   131→
   132→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
   133→/* The single constructor surface (both provenance origins)             */
   134→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
   135→
   136→/** The authoring input of `createOperationIntent` — semantics + provenance. */
   137→export interface CreateOperationIntentInput {
   138→  readonly intentId: string;
   139→  readonly operationType: string;
   140→  readonly domain: SolutionDomainDescriptor;
   141→  readonly parameters: readonly TypedOperationParameter[];
   142→  readonly target: OperationTarget;
   143→  readonly dependsOn?: readonly OperationDependency[];
   144→  readonly provenance: OperationProvenance;
   145→  readonly proposedTo?: IntentProposalContext;
   146→}
   147→
   148→function toIssues(error: z.ZodError): SolutionContractIssue[] {
   149→  return error.issues.map((issue) => ({
   150→    path: [...issue.path],
   151→    message: issue.message,
   152→    code: issue.code,
   153→  }));
   154→}
   155→
   156→/**
   157→ * THE single constructor surface for operation intents (PROD-021 §4.2:
   158→ * "one constructor surface, two provenance origins"). Pure and
   159→ * deterministic:
   160→ *
   161→ *  - stamps the current contract version on the intent and its embedded
   162→ *    wire objects (domain, target, dependencies) — the constructor is the
   163→ *    authoring surface, wire values with foreign versions must be DECODED,
   164→ *    not reconstructed;
   165→ *  - validates the full wire schema (typed `SolutionContractEncodeError`
   166→ *    on any violation) AND the cross-field invariants of
   167→ *    `checkEngineeringOperationIntent` (units, anchoring, provenance) — the
   168→ *    constructor can only emit contract-valid intents;
   169→ *  - accepts either provenance origin verbatim: the same semantic input
   170→ *    with `origin: "direct-manipulation"` or `origin: "agent"` yields
   171→ *    intents whose semantic fields are deep-equal and whose derived
   172→ *    operation identity is IDENTICAL.
   173→ */
   174→export function createOperationIntent(
   175→  input: CreateOperationIntentInput,
   176→): EngineeringOperationIntent {
   177→  const context = { family: "operation" as const, objectName: "EngineeringOperationIntent" };
   178→  const candidate = {
   179→    contractVersion: SOLUTION_CONTRACT_VERSION,
   180→    intentId: input.intentId,
   181→    operationType: input.operationType,
   182→    domain: { ...input.domain, contractVersion: SOLUTION_CONTRACT_VERSION },
   183→    parameters: input.parameters,
   184→    target: { ...input.target, contractVersion: SOLUTION_CONTRACT_VERSION },
   185→    dependsOn: (input.dependsOn ?? []).map((dependency) => ({
   186→      ...dependency,
   187→      contractVersion: SOLUTION_CONTRACT_VERSION,
   188→    })),
   189→    provenance: input.provenance,
   190→    proposedTo: input.proposedTo,
   191→  };
   192→  const parsed = EngineeringOperationIntentSchema.safeParse(candidate);
   193→  if (!parsed.success) {
   194→    throw new SolutionContractEncodeError(context, toIssues(parsed.error));
   195→  }
   196→  // The constructor is the authoring boundary: run the invariant checks
   197→  // (numeric-without-unit, unanchored target, missing provenance) so only
   198→  // contract-valid intents can be constructed.
   199→  const findings = checkEngineeringOperationIntent(parsed.data);
   200→  if (findings.length > 0) {
   201→    throw new SolutionContractEncodeError(
   202→      context,
   203→      findings.map((finding) => ({
   204→        path: [...finding.path],
   205→        message: `${finding.code}: ${finding.detail}`,
   206→        code: finding.code,
   207→      })),
   208→    );
   209→  }
   210→  return parsed.data;
   211→}
