1→/**
     2→ * Engineering operation record and satellites (PROD-021) — family `operation`.
     3→ *
     4→ * The typed, reproducible `EngineeringOperation` of ACR-005/006: every
     5→ * consequential interaction of the interactive solution workflow resolves to
     6→ * one of these records with:
     7→ *
     8→ *  - operation identity and version context (`operationId`, `solutionId`,
     9→ *    `versionNumber`, `operationIndex`);
    10→ *  - operation type and explicit typed parameters WITH UNITS;
    11→ *  - a stable spatial `OperationTarget` anchored to observed reality through
    12→ *    READ-ONLY references;
    13→ *  - precedence/dependency edges (`OperationDependency`);
    14→ *  - engine-derived effects (`OperationEffect`: proposed state transitions
    15→ *    and quantity impacts with typed units and calculation provenance);
    16→ *  - source and provenance (`OperationProvenance`: direct manipulation,
    17→ *    agent command or imported template — attribution, evidence, the exact
    18→ *    normalized agent command).
    19→ *
    20→ * DESIGN NOTE — PLAIN WIRE SCHEMAS: cross-field invariants (numeric
    21→ * parameters require a unit; targets must anchor; provenance must be
    22→ * present; no self-dependency) are NOT expressed as zod refinements. The
    23→ * wire schemas are plain `.passthrough()` objects — the discipline shared
    24→ * with `@aise/shared-contracts`/`@aise/adapter-contract` that keeps the
    25→ * strict-decode schema walker sound — and the invariants ship as typed
    26→ * checker functions in `src/invariants.ts` (the boundary-parser discipline
    27→ * of the intervention model). See this package's README.
    28→ *
    29→ * The operation record is ENGINE-OWNED (PROD-022): clients and agents author
    30→ * intents (see intent.ts); the solution engine compiles intents into
    31→ * operation records and derives their effects deterministically.
    32→ */
    33→
    34→import { z } from "zod";
    35→import {
    36→  UncertaintySchema,
    37→  contractVersionSchema,
    38→  contentIdSchema,
    39→  isoTimestampSchema,
    40→  positiveIntSchema,
    41→  shortTextSchema,
    42→  stableIdSchema,
    43→  textSchema,
    44→} from "@aise/shared-contracts";
    45→import { createSolutionWireCodec } from "./codec";
    46→import { SolutionDomainDescriptorSchema } from "./domain";
    47→
    48→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
    49→/* Typed parameters (explicit units — never bare numbers)               */
    50→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
    51→
    52→/**
    53→ * One typed operation parameter. `unit` is REQUIRED for numeric values — the
    54→ * frozen numeric-value-requires-a-typed-unit discipline of the Reality Graph
    55→ * and intervention models (checked by invariants.ts:
    56→ * `numeric_parameter_without_unit`). Non-numeric values (material names,
    57→ * boolean options) carry no unit.
    58→ */
    59→export const TypedOperationParameterSchema = z
    60→  .object({
    61→    name: shortTextSchema.describe(
    62→      "Parameter name (open vocabulary, lower-kebab-case; e.g. depth, width, " +
    63→        "length, thickness, height, diameter, material).",
    64→    ),
    65→    value: z
    66→      .union([z.number(), z.string(), z.boolean()])
    67→      .describe(
    68→        "The parameter value. Numeric values REQUIRE an explicit unit; " +
    69→          "string values carry named choices (e.g. material) without units.",
    70→      ),
    71→    unit: shortTextSchema
    72→      .optional()
    73→      .describe(
    74→        "Explicit unit for numeric values (e.g. m, mm). REQUIRED for " +
    75→          "numeric values (invariant numeric_parameter_without_unit); " +
    76→          "absent for non-numeric values.",
    77→      ),
    78→  })
    79→  .passthrough();
    80→export type TypedOperationParameter = z.infer<typeof TypedOperationParameterSchema>;
    81→
    82→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
    83→/* Operation provenance (attribution + evidence + command)              */
    84→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
    85→
    86→/**
    87→ * The authoring origins of an operation intent: direct manipulation in the
    88→ * interactive environment, an agent command (translated to the same typed
    89→ * semantics — ACR-005 "two equivalent input modes"), or an imported
    90→ * template. Open vocabulary beyond the three advisory values.
    91→ */
    92→export const OPERATION_INTENT_ORIGINS = [
    93→  "direct-manipulation",
    94→  "agent",
    95→  "imported-template",
    96→] as const;
    97→export type OperationIntentOrigin = (typeof OPERATION_INTENT_ORIGINS)[number];
    98→
    99→/**
   100→ * Provenance of one operation/intent: WHO authored it, WHEN, from WHAT
   101→ * evidence, and — for agent origin — the EXACT normalized command text that
   102→ * compiled to it (PROD-023 preserves it verbatim). At least one of
   103→ * `evidenceIds` (non-empty), `derivationNote` or `commandText` must be
   104→ * present (invariant `missing_operation_provenance`) — attribution is never
   105→ * optional, and attribution is NEVER part of operation identity (see
   106→ * identity.ts: the same semantics authored by direct manipulation or an
   107→ * agent IS the same operation).
   108→ */
   109→export const OperationProvenanceSchema = z
   110→  .object({
   111→    origin: z
   112→      .enum(OPERATION_INTENT_ORIGINS)
   113→      .describe(
   114→        "How the operation was authored: direct-manipulation (interactive " +
   115→          "environment), agent (natural-language command compiled to the " +
   116→          "same typed semantics) or imported-template.",
   117→      ),
   118→    authoredBy: shortTextSchema.describe(
   119→      "Stable reference of the author: user id, agent id or template id.",
   120→    ),
   121→    authoredAt: isoTimestampSchema.describe(
   122→      "Instant the intent was authored (excluded from identity derivations).",
   123→    ),
   124→    commandText: textSchema
   125→      .optional()
   126→      .describe(
   127→        "agent origin: the EXACT normalized natural-language command that " +
   128→          "compiled to this operation — carried verbatim, never paraphrased.",
   129→      ),
   130→    interactionDetail: shortTextSchema
   131→      .optional()
   132→      .describe(
   133→        "direct-manipulation origin: the manipulation description (e.g. " +
   134→          "'operator dragged excavation volume handles in the 3D view').",
   135→      ),
   136→    evidenceIds: z
   137→      .array(contentIdSchema)
   138→      .describe(
   139→        "Input evidence content ids (64-hex Evidence-Graph addresses); " +
   140→          "may be empty when a derivation note or command text states the " +
   141→          "provenance.",
   142→      ),
   143→    derivationNote: textSchema
   144→      .optional()
   145→      .describe(
   146→        "Explicit derivation/attribution statement when no evidence id " +
   147→          "applies (e.g. 'operator dimensioned the volume directly in the " +
   148→          "interactive 3D view').",
   149→      ),
   150→    intentRef: stableIdSchema
   151→      .optional()
   152→      .describe(
   153→        "OPERATION RECORDS ONLY: the intent event that authored this " +
   154→          "operation (the compile provenance link of PROD-022/023).",
   155→      ),
   156→  })
   157→  .passthrough();
   158→export type OperationProvenance = z.infer<typeof OperationProvenanceSchema>;
   159→
   160→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
   161→/* OperationTarget (stable spatial target)                              */
   162→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
   163→
   164→/**
   165→ * How a spatial target selects space. Open-ended towards vertical-specific
   166→ * selectors while staying geometry-kind-neutral.
   167→ */
   168→export const SPATIAL_SELECTOR_KINDS = [
   169→  "element",
   170→  "face-set",
   171→  "surface-region",
   172→  "volume",
   173→  "line-extent",
   174→  "point",
   175→  "storey",
   176→  "space",
   177→] as const;
   178→export type SpatialSelectorKind = (typeof SPATIAL_SELECTOR_KINDS)[number];
   179→
   180→/**
   181→ * Geometry reference kinds — mirroring the Reality Graph's geometry-ref
   182→ * discipline: geometry is REFERENCED, never embedded here; computation is
   183→ * owned by the deterministic geometry services (PROD-022).
   184→ */
   185→export const TARGET_GEOMETRY_REF_KINDS = [
   186→  "plane",
   187→  "polygon",
   188→  "mesh-ref",
   189→  "point-cloud-ref",
   190→] as const;
   191→export type TargetGeometryRefKind = (typeof TARGET_GEOMETRY_REF_KINDS)[number];
   192→
   193→export const TargetGeometryRefSchema = z
   194→  .object({
   195→    kind: z.enum(TARGET_GEOMETRY_REF_KINDS),
   196→    ref: stableIdSchema.describe(
   197→      "Stable id of the referenced geometry artifact (owned by the " +
   198→        "deterministic geometry services; read-only reference).",
   199→    ),
   200→  })
   201→  .passthrough();
   202→export type TargetGeometryRef = z.infer<typeof TargetGeometryRefSchema>;
   203→
   204→/** Units of a target's spatial anchors (linear/angular, carried verbatim). */
   205→export const SpatialUnitsSchema = z
   206→  .object({
   207→    linear: shortTextSchema.describe("Linear unit of the target's anchors (e.g. m)."),
   208→    angular: shortTextSchema.describe("Angular unit of the target's anchors (e.g. rad)."),
   209→  })
   210→  .passthrough();
   211→export type SpatialUnits = z.infer<typeof SpatialUnitsSchema>;
   212→
   213→/**
   214→ * The stable spatial target of an operation: a selector over Reality-Graph
   215→ * nodes and/or deterministic geometry references, with explicit units and a
   216→ * human-readable description. `nodeRefs` and `geometryRefs` are READ-ONLY
   217→ * references to OBSERVED reality and engine geometry — an operation never
   218→ * mutates them. At least one node or geometry reference must anchor the
   219→ * target (invariant `unanchored_operation_target`).
   220→ */
   221→export const OperationTargetSchema = z
   222→  .object({
   223→    contractVersion: contractVersionSchema,
   224→    selectorKind: z
   225→      .enum(SPATIAL_SELECTOR_KINDS)
   226→      .describe(
   227→        "How the target selects space: element (whole node), face-set " +
   228→          "(element faces), surface-region, volume, line-extent, point, " +
   229→          "storey or space.",
   230→      ),
   231→    nodeRefs: z
   232→      .array(stableIdSchema)
   233→      .describe(
   234→        "Stable Reality Graph node ids the target anchors to (read-only " +
   235→          "references to observed reality).",
   236→      ),
   237→    geometryRefs: z
   238→      .array(TargetGeometryRefSchema)
   239→      .describe(
   240→        "Deterministic geometry references anchoring or limiting the " +
   241→          "target (drawn pit outlines, wall face polygons…).",
   242→      ),
   243→    units: SpatialUnitsSchema.describe(
   244→      "Units of the spatial coordinates/anchors (carried verbatim).",
   245→    ),
   246→    description: shortTextSchema.describe(
   247→      "Human-readable place description (e.g. 'the affected wall faces'); " +
   248→        "presentation only — excluded from identity derivations.",
   249→    ),
   250→  })
   251→  .passthrough();
   252→export type OperationTarget = z.infer<typeof OperationTargetSchema>;
   253→
   254→export const OperationTargetCodec = createSolutionWireCodec<OperationTarget>({
   255→  name: "OperationTarget",
   256→  family: "operation",
   257→  schema: OperationTargetSchema,
   258→});
   259→export const decodeOperationTarget = OperationTargetCodec.decode;
   260→export const decodeOperationTargetStrict = OperationTargetCodec.decodeStrict;
   261→export const encodeOperationTarget = OperationTargetCodec.encode;
   262→
   263→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
   264→/* OperationDependency (precedence/dependency edges)                    */
   265→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
   266→
   267→/** Dependency semantics: what must hold before this operation may apply. */
   268→export const OPERATION_DEPENDENCY_KINDS = [
   269→  "completion-before",
   270→  "state-precondition",
   271→] as const;
   272→export type OperationDependencyKind = (typeof OPERATION_DEPENDENCY_KINDS)[number];
   273→
   274→/**
   275→ * One precedence/dependency edge: this operation depends on the referenced
   276→ * operation either completing first (`completion-before`) or producing a
   277→ * precondition proposed state (`state-precondition`). An operation never
   278→ * depends on itself (invariant `self_referencing_operation_dependency`).
   279→ */
   280→export const OperationDependencySchema = z
   281→  .object({
   282→    contractVersion: contractVersionSchema,
   283→    operationRef: stableIdSchema.describe(
   284→      "The operation this dependency points at (its completion or its " +
   285→        "resulting proposed state is the precondition).",
   286→    ),
   287→    dependencyKind: z.enum(OPERATION_DEPENDENCY_KINDS),
   288→    rationale: textSchema
   289→      .optional()
   290→      .describe("Why the dependency exists (presentation; excluded from identity)."),
   291→  })
   292→  .passthrough();
   293→export type OperationDependency = z.infer<typeof OperationDependencySchema>;
   294→
   295→export const OperationDependencyCodec = createSolutionWireCodec<OperationDependency>({
   296→  name: "OperationDependency",
   297→  family: "operation",
   298→  schema: OperationDependencySchema,
   299→});
   300→export const decodeOperationDependency = OperationDependencyCodec.decode;
   301→export const decodeOperationDependencyStrict = OperationDependencyCodec.decodeStrict;
   302→export const encodeOperationDependency = OperationDependencyCodec.encode;
   303→
   304→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
   305→/* Quantities (typed units + calculation provenance + uncertainty)      */
   306→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
   307→
   308→/** Quantity dimensions of the initial building operation library. */
   309→export const QUANTITY_DIMENSIONS = [
   310→  "length",
   311→  "area",
   312→  "volume",
   313→  "mass",
   314→  "count",
   315→  "duration",
   316→] as const;
   317→export type QuantityDimension = (typeof QUANTITY_DIMENSIONS)[number];
   318→
   319→/** Whether a quantity is added, removed or changed by an operation. */
   320→export const QUANTITY_IMPACT_DIRECTIONS = ["added", "removed", "changed"] as const;
   321→export type QuantityImpactDirection = (typeof QUANTITY_IMPACT_DIRECTIONS)[number];
   322→
   323→/**
   324→ * A typed quantity with an EXPLICIT unit (never a bare number), the
   325→ * calculation reference that produced it (calculation provenance —
   326→ * ACR-005's "units, calculation method") and optional propagated
   327→ * measurement uncertainty. Uncertainty is carried VERBATIM from the
   328→ * underlying properties (the AISE-013/AISE-028 first-order propagation
   329→ * discipline); it is never fabricated here.
   330→ */
   331→export const TypedQuantitySchema = z
   332→  .object({
   333→    dimension: z.enum(QUANTITY_DIMENSIONS),
   334→    value: z.number().describe("Quantity value in the stated unit."),
   335→    unit: shortTextSchema.describe(
   336→      "Explicit unit (REQUIRED — a quantity is never a bare number).",
   337→    ),
   338→    calculationRef: shortTextSchema.describe(
   339→      "Reference to the deterministic calculation/method that produced the " +
   340→        "value (calculation provenance).",
   341→    ),
   342→    uncertainty: UncertaintySchema
   343→      .optional()
   344→      .describe(
   345→        "Propagated measurement uncertainty where stated; absent means " +
   346→          "'not stated' — never zero, never fabricated.",
   347→      ),
   348→  })
   349→  .passthrough();
   350→export type TypedQuantity = z.infer<typeof TypedQuantitySchema>;
   351→
   352→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
   353→/* OperationEffect (state deltas + quantity impacts)                    */
   354→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
   355→
   356→export const OPERATION_EFFECT_KINDS = ["state-transition", "quantity-impact"] as const;
   357→export type OperationEffectKind = (typeof OPERATION_EFFECT_KINDS)[number];
   358→
   359→/**
   360→ * One engine-derived effect of an operation: either a `state-transition`
   361→ * (the `ProposedState` this operation's application produces — requires
   362→ * `resultingStateRef`) or a `quantity-impact` (a typed quantity the
   363→ * operation adds/removes/changes — requires `quantity` and `direction`).
   364→ * Both members are checked by invariants.ts (`operation_effect_missing_ref`
   365→ * / `operation_effect_missing_quantity`). Effects are DERIVED outputs of
   366→ * the deterministic solution engine (PROD-022) and are deliberately
   367→ * EXCLUDED from operation identity (identity.ts).
   368→ */
   369→export const OperationEffectSchema = z
   370→  .object({
   371→    contractVersion: contractVersionSchema,
   372→    effectKind: z.enum(OPERATION_EFFECT_KINDS),
   373→    resultingStateRef: stableIdSchema
   374→      .optional()
   375→      .describe(
   376→        "state-transition: the id of the ProposedState this operation's " +
   377→          "application produces (states[N] after operation N).",
   378→      ),
   379→    quantity: TypedQuantitySchema
   380→      .optional()
   381→      .describe("quantity-impact: the typed quantity this operation affects."),
   382→    direction: z
   383→      .enum(QUANTITY_IMPACT_DIRECTIONS)
   384→      .optional()
   385→      .describe(
   386→        "quantity-impact: whether the quantity is added, removed or changed.",
   387→      ),
   388→    affectedNodeRefs: z
   389→      .array(stableIdSchema)
   390→      .describe(
   391→        "Reality nodes the effect touches (read-only references to " +
   392→          "observed reality).",
   393→      ),
   394→    geometryRefs: z
   395→      .array(TargetGeometryRefSchema)
   396→      .describe(
   397→        "Geometry references the effect's state delta or quantity derives " +
   398→          "from.",
   399→      ),
   400→  })
   401→  .passthrough();
   402→export type OperationEffect = z.infer<typeof OperationEffectSchema>;
   403→
   404→export const OperationEffectCodec = createSolutionWireCodec<OperationEffect>({
   405→  name: "OperationEffect",
   406→  family: "operation",
   407→  schema: OperationEffectSchema,
   408→});
   409→export const decodeOperationEffect = OperationEffectCodec.decode;
   410→export const decodeOperationEffectStrict = OperationEffectCodec.decodeStrict;
   411→export const encodeOperationEffect = OperationEffectCodec.encode;
   412→
   413→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
   414→/* EngineeringOperation (the recorded operation)                        */
   415→/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
   416→
   417→/**
   418→ * A recorded engineering operation of a solution version: the typed,
   419→ * parameterized, spatially anchored, reproducible unit of the Solution
   420→ * Graph (ACR-005/006). `operationId` is the DETERMINISTIC identity
   421→ * (identity.ts `deriveEngineeringOperationId` — content-addressed over the
   422→ * semantic projection, version-context-pinned, provenance-EXCLUDED).
   423→ * `operationType` is an open wire string; the closed Phase 1 building
   424→ * catalogue (`BUILDING_OPERATION_TYPES`) is engine-owned reference data.
   425→ */
   426→export const EngineeringOperationSchema = z
   427→  .object({
   428→    contractVersion: contractVersionSchema,
   429→    operationId: stableIdSchema.describe(
   430→      "Deterministic operation identity (deriveEngineeringOperationId): " +
   431→        "sha-256 over the canonical semantic projection — same semantics " +
   432→        "(type, parameters, target, dependencies, version context) yield " +
   433→        "the same id regardless of authoring origin.",
   434→    ),
   435→    solutionId: stableIdSchema.describe("The solution this operation belongs to."),
   436→    versionNumber: positiveIntSchema.describe(
   437→      "The solution version this operation is recorded in (version " +
   438→        "context — part of operation identity).",
   439→    ),
   440→    operationIndex: positiveIntSchema.describe(
   441→      "1-based position of this operation in its version's ordered " +
   442→        "sequence (order is semantic: it is hashed into identity and " +
   443→        "state ids).",
   444→    ),
   445→    operationType: shortTextSchema.describe(
   446→      "The operation type (OPEN vocabulary; Phase 1 building advisory " +
   447→        "values: BUILDING_OPERATION_TYPES of the domain module).",
   448→    ),
   449→    domain: SolutionDomainDescriptorSchema.describe(
   450→      "The vertical context of the operation — building specifics live " +
   451→        "here as DATA, never as client authority.",
   452→    ),
   453→    parameters: z
   454→      .array(TypedOperationParameterSchema)
   455→      .min(1)
   456→      .describe(
   457→        "The explicit typed parameters (with units) — at least one; a " +
   458→          "parameterless operation is not representable.",
   459→      ),
   460→    target: OperationTargetSchema.describe(
   461→      "The stable spatial target, anchored to observed reality through " +
   462→        "read-only references.",
   463→    ),
   464→    dependsOn: z
   465→      .array(OperationDependencySchema)
   466→      .describe(
   467→        "Precedence/dependency edges to other operations (may be empty).",
   468→      ),
   469→    effects: z
   470→      .array(OperationEffectSchema)
   471→      .describe(
   472→        "Engine-derived effects: proposed state transitions and quantity " +
   473→          "impacts (deterministic outputs of PROD-022; excluded from " +
   474→          "identity).",
   475→      ),
   476→    provenance: OperationProvenanceSchema.describe(
   477→      "Authoring attribution: origin (direct-manipulation | agent | " +
   478→        "imported-template), author, instant, evidence, exact agent " +
   479→        "command, compile intent reference.",
   480→    ),
   481→    rationale: textSchema
   482→      .optional()
   483→      .describe(
   484→        "Free-text rationale (presentation; excluded from identity " +
   485→          "derivations).",
   486→      ),
   487→  })
   488→  .passthrough();
   489→export type EngineeringOperation = z.infer<typeof EngineeringOperationSchema>;
   490→
   491→export const EngineeringOperationCodec =
   492→  createSolutionWireCodec<EngineeringOperation>({
   493→    name: "EngineeringOperation",

1→# PROD-017 — browser task trace (the golden journey through the real entrypoints)
     2→
     3→**Work item:** PROD-017 (browser adapter and task-first product UX)
     4→**Base:** public main @ `7d21d47147a3df14a0e6138131de6d9add672d27`
     5→
     6→The trace below is the golden journey as the **automated task trace**
     7→(`apps/web/src/app/golden-journey.test.tsx`) drives it: the app's REAL
     8→entrypoints — the typed hash router, the same-origin API seam (`app/api.ts`),
     9→the task-first adapter modules, the shell/viewer projections — with only the
    10→fetch transport injected (the `api.test.ts` discipline: fixed stub payloads,
    11→no network, no clock, no randomness). The `/v1/adapter/**` stub bodies are
    12→the committed PROD-016 corpus values — exactly what a contract-serving
    13→deployment answers; the `/v1/**` stub bodies are the backend's own record
    14→contracts.
    15→
    16→The journey is executable in the browser without source-code/API knowledge:
    17→the landing asks **"What do you need to do?"**, the task intent is authored
    18→through a form, and every subsequent screen exposes the next useful action
    19→or an explicit blocked reason.
    20→
    21→---
    22→
    23→## Step 0 — the journey's addresses (the router entrypoint)
    24→
    25→`parseHash` (the app's pure route codec) resolves every journey address:
    26→`#/` → dashboard (the task-first landing), `#/projects` → the open/create
    27→surface, `#/projects/proj-7f3a2b` → project overview,
    28→`…/sitetwin` → evidence, `…/boq-lens` → BOQ, `…/case` → the case,
    29→`…/intervention?layer=3&scenario=scenario-55c1` → the intervention studio.
    30→No second navigation model exists: the journey steps (`GOLDEN_JOURNEY_STEPS`
    31→in `task-flow.ts`) project onto these same routes.
    32→
    33→## Step 1 — open / create the project (the identity entrypoints)
    34→
    35→- **Read:** `GET /v1/identity/organizations/org-northwind/projects?requester=user-alice`
    36→  (requester-guarded) → `ProjectRecord[]`; `proj-7f3a2b` (Riverside Block B
    37→  Refurbishment) is the current project.
    38→- **Write:** `POST /v1/identity/organizations/org-northwind/projects` with the
    39→  identity router's exact body `{ projectId, name, actor }` → the created
    40→  record.
    41→- *Semantics observed:* the project registry is server-owned; the adapter
    42→  renders records verbatim and never re-keys them.
    43→
    44→## Step 2 — author the task intent (W-R3) and submit it (the adapter seam)
    45→
    46→The user's statement — *"Capture depth evidence of the cracked masonry on
    47→level 2 so the engineering case can be diagnosed."* — is assembled by
    48→`taskIntentFromSelection` into a typed **`TaskIntent`** wire object
    49→(`taskType: field-capture`, `projectRef: proj-7f3a2b`, `targetRefs:
    50→[case-91ab, node-wall-12]`, `parameters: {priority: high, area: level-2}`,
    51→`createdAt: 2026-01-15T09:25:00.000Z`) — the ONE client-authored semantic
    52→object. `POST /v1/adapter/task-intents` answers the
    53→**server-authoritative `OperationResult`**:

Wait — one important consideration about React testing. The existing web tests use `renderToStaticMarkup` from "react-dom/server" — I saw it imported in golden-journey.test.tsx. That's the house testing pattern (no DOM environment, just static markup + props callbacks). I'll follow that: components are mostly presentational with props/callbacks; the STATE LOGIC is a pure reducer in model.ts that tests drive directly; component tests use renderToStaticMarkup to assert rendered structure (a11y roles/labels, observed-vs-proposed distinction, refusal surfacing).

For interactivity, the component uses useReducer + callbacks — all testable via the reducer + static markup assertions.

**The key seams (ports):**

{"content": "# PROD-024 — Mutation-protection evidence (proposed reality cannot overwrite authoritative reality)

**Work item:** PROD-024 · **Module:** `apps/web/src/solution/**`
**Source:** the automated suites
(`apps/web/src/solution/workspace.test.tsx` — "PROD-024 mutation
protection"; `operations.test.ts`; `viewer/viewer.test.ts`).

The workspace enforces the §4.3 doctrine STRUCTURALLY — no UI path can
mutate the authoritative reality — and the engine's refusals are surfaced
honestly. The evidence, per guarantee:

## 1. There is NO client-side write path to observed reality

- The observed scene is READ-ONLY display data received via props
  (`SolutionCaseContext.observedScene`); the workspace state model
  (`model.ts`) has NO action that touches it, and no observed-layer write
  exists anywhere in the module (the boundary is structural, not
  conventional).
- **Test:** "the OBSERVED scene is never mutated by any interaction" — a
  deep clone of the scene taken before the full golden journey
  (direct manipulation + agent turns + revision) is deep-equal to the
  scene after it.

## 2. PROPOSED states are structurally sealed apart from OBSERVED reality

- Every proposed layer is an ENGINE-materialized `ProposedState` — the
  schema-level `epistemicStatus: "PROPOSED"` literal and the read-only
  `baselineRealityVersionId` pin (the contract's proposal-isolation seal;
  OBSERVED/INFERRED/CONFIRMED are unrepresentable inside a proposal).
- **Test:** "every proposed state carries the PROPOSED seal over the
  PINNED baseline" — every state of every version in the journey's
  history asserts the seal and the pinned `rgv-demo-0007`.
- **Viewer evidence:** the SVG renders two STRUCTURALLY distinct layer
  groups (`<g data-layer="observed" data-epistemic-class="OBSERVED">`
  vs `<g data-layer="proposed" data-epistemic-class="PROPOSED">`); an
  observed element can never render inside the proposed group (asserted
  by the viewer suite's layer-separation test).

## 3. Every mutation flows through the engine's lifecycle (draft → … ;
   revision is versioning, never rewriting)

- The ONLY mutation surface is `submitIntent` (the one submission path)
  which calls the engine service; the ONLY undo surface is
  `reviseOperation` which calls the engine's revision service.
- **Test:** "revision preserves the prior version VERBATIM (append-only
  history)" — after the golden journey's revision, version 1 is still in
  the history deep-equal to its pre-revision snapshot; the history holds
  both versions.
- **Test:** "TIMELINE DETERMINISM: stepping equals the ENGINE's replay
  byte-for-byte" — the workspace-evolved version 2 is canonically
  byte-identical to the ENGINE's `replaySolution` output over the same
  intents (deterministic replay, not a client-side snapshot hack); every
  timeline cursor position lands on exactly the engine's recorded states.

## 4. Attempt-to-overwrite-authoritative operations are REFUSED by the
   engine and the UI surfaces the refusal honestly

- **Test:** "an attempt to overwrite authoritative reality (cross-solution
  intent) is REFUSED and surfaced honestly" — a hostile intent proposing
  into ANOTHER solution (`proposedTo: solution-other-999`) is refused by
  the engine with `baseline_mismatch` ("an intent is never silently
  re-targeted"); the workspace records ZERO applied operations, surfaces
  the typed notice (source `solution-engine`, outcome `invalid`, the
  machine-readable reason verbatim) and the journey records the refusal
  ("…the solution engine REFUSED … nothing was applied").
- **Test:** "an underspecified operation is refused with needs-input" — a
  demolition missing height/thickness answers `needs-input` with
  `missing_required_parameter` (the engine ASKS, never invents).
- **Test:** "an operation outside the engine catalogue is refused as
  unsupported" — a future-vertical operation (trench shoring) answers
  `unsupported` with `capability_unsupported` (explicit, never silent).
- The contract constructor itself refuses non-PROPOSED epistemic claims
  structurally (the PROD-021 authority suite); the workspace offers no
  authoring field that could carry one.

## 5. The BOQ projection never overwrites a source BOQ

- The BOQ seam is strictly read-only over the contract's trace-set wire
  object; when the trace set pins another version than the one being
  viewed, the pane reports the pin honestly ("never silently re-keyed") —
  **Test:** "the BOQ guard: v1 data syncs at v1 and reports the pin
  honestly after the revision" + "no BOQ data → the honest none state
  (never a crash, never fabricated lines)".

## 6. Revision of a terminal version / unknown target refuses honestly

- The engine's revision refusals (`version_terminal`,
  `unknown_operation_to_revert`, `revision_not_appendable`) flow through
  the same notice surface (the revision-refused notice kind; exercised by
  the engine's own suite, consumed verbatim here).
", "filepath": "/home/z/AISE/docs/productization-evidence/PROD-024/mutation-protection-evidence.md"}

{"content": "# PROD-024 — Accessibility / fallback trace (the first-class non-viewer path)

**Work item:** PROD-024 · **Module:** `apps/web/src/solution/**`
**Source:** the automated suites
(`apps/web/src/solution/fallback/fallback.test.tsx` — headless
completeness + markup accessibility; `workspace.test.tsx` — the component
surfaces; the WCAG-AA stylesheet in `styles.ts`).

The accessible non-3D fallback is a FIRST-CLASS path (§4.7): a user can
inspect and revise a full solution through it, with zero reliance on the
spatial viewer — and it exercises the SAME semantics.

## 1. Headless completeness (the fallback session, no viewer involved)

The recorded fallback session (automated; the exact controllers the
fallback panes call — no scene SVG, no projection anywhere in the path):

```text
1. inspect   — the workspace opens on the engine baseline overlay
               (version 1, layer 0, PROPOSED seal, pinned rgv-demo-0007).
2. select    — the user selects the damaged wall faces through the
               ACCESSIBLE scene list (a labeled button list — not the
               drawing).
3. manipulate — "Remove the damaged section" (demolition 5 m × 2.4 m ×
               0.1 m) through the SAME typed-intent path: engine applies,
               layer 1 materializes with the corpus's operation identity.
4. step      — timeline back to layer 0, forward to layer 1 (engine
               states by identity).
5. inspect   — the operation's detail record (parameters, target,
               provenance, state delta, engine quantities).
6. revise    — "Undo this step (new version)": NEW version 2 through the
               engine's revision service; version 1 preserved verbatim in
               the history.
```

The journey record of that session (asserted):
`[inspect, direct-manipulation, step-back, step-forward, revise]` — every
step traceable without any spatial rendering. An agent decision
(unsupported) also folds through the fallback path with the verbatim
reason surfaced (asserted).

## 2. The accessible scene pane (markup, asserted)

- every observed element renders as a **labeled button** with
  `aria-pressed` selection state and its recorded facts (e.g. "Observed
  area (south face set): 12.5 m2");
- the proposed work at the current step renders as a **labeled list**
  with real-world wording, step numbers and directions ("Removed section
  — removes material (Removing a section, step 1)");
- explicit empty states ("No proposed work is visible at this step.").

## 3. Keyboard navigation and screen-reader labeling (markup, asserted)

| Surface | Accessibility affordances (asserted) |
|---|---|
| Workspace root | `aria-label="Interactive solution workspace — …"`, `role`-bearing semantic landmarks (`main`/`header`/`footer`/`section`) |
| Timeline | prev/next buttons with `aria-label`s; every layer tick is a button with a full `aria-label` ("Layer 1: …; removes 1.2 m3 …") and `aria-current="step"` at the cursor |
| Operation list | every row is a button with the full real-world summary + provenance in its `aria-label` |
| Detail inspector | a labeled region (`aria-label="Details of step N"`), definition rows (`dl`), the verbatim command quote, and the undo control's explicit `aria-label` ("creates a new version, keeps history") |
| Quantities | a real `<table>` with `<caption>` and `scope="col"` headers |
| Notice pane | `role="status"` + `aria-live="polite"` |
| Agent panel | a programmatic label on the input (`sr-only` + `for`/`id`), a live transcript (`role="log"` + `aria-live="polite"`), pending states as visible cards with explicit confirm/cancel buttons |
| Viewer | `role="img"` + `aria-label` + the textual scene alternative (observed and proposed content in words); all controls are native buttons/inputs/selects/sliders with labels |
| Fallback toggle | an `aria-pressed` button ("Use the accessible view (no drawing)") |

## 4. WCAG AA contrast and focus (stylesheet)

The module's stylesheet (a constant string, never data-derived) keeps:
body text `#1c1917` on `#ffffff` (≈16:1), secondary text `#57534e`
(≈7.4:1), refusal tones `#7f1d1d` on `#fef2f2` (≈7:1), pending-proposal
`#134e4a`-family borders on `#f0fdfa`; every interactive element carries
an explicit `:focus-visible` outline (`#c2410c`, 3px) for keyboard users;
buttons keep comfortable touch targets (≥34px control height, ≥44px rows
via padding); the observed/proposed color distinction is always PAIRED
with the structural layer separation + dash patterns + textual
alternatives (never color alone).

## 5. The fallback is not a stub

The fallback session above performs a COMPLETE inspect-and-revise cycle:
select → manipulate → step → inspect detail → undo — all through the same
typed intents, the same one submission path, the same engine states and
the same append-only revision as the viewer path (the convergence is the
point: there is exactly one operation semantics in the module).
", "filepath": "/home/z/AISE/docs/productization-evidence/PROD-024/accessibility-fallback-trace.md"}
